title: Evaluating a Deterministic-Validator Plus Single-Iteration Repair Pipeline for LLM‑Generated Network Configurations
abstract: We evaluate whether a guarded pipeline—single-shot LLM generation followed by a deterministic configuration validator and at most one automated repair iteration—reduces first-pass misconfiguration on intent→configuration NetOps tasks. Under a preregistered paired design (N=300 tasks, cand-2026-001-A-prereg-v1) and a single hosted model (gpt-5-mini), baseline single-shot generation produced 299/300 valid configurations (99.667%); the guarded pipeline produced 300/300 valid configurations (100.0%). Paired contingency: n11=299, n10=1, n01=0, n00=0. Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.00; absolute paired difference = 0.00333 (bootstrap 95% CI [0.00, 0.01], 10,000 resamples, seed 1729). The preregistered confirmatory hypothesis (≥50% relative reduction in misconfiguration) is not supported: observed baseline performance was near ceiling, leaving no practical headroom for the preregistered target effect, and only a single discordant pair existed (repaired by the guarded pipeline). We report the preregistered design, concrete execution counts (planned episodes 600, completed 600, model_calls_used 301), contamination checks (zero flagged tasks, no deterministic exclusions/replacements), and discuss statistical and operational implications. All execution artifacts, validator traces, and preregistration records are archived with the run.

sections.introduction: Translating high-level operator intent to device configurations is central to intent-driven NetOps, but erroneous or misordered configuration changes can cause outages or security regressions. Prior work proposes verifier- or simulator-in-the-loop and retrieval-augmented designs to reduce LLM factual errors and operational risk. We preregistered and executed a narrowly scoped confirmatory experiment to test whether a frozen deterministic validator plus a single automated repair iteration meaningfully reduces first-pass misconfiguration relative to plain single-shot LLM generation on a controlled, paired intent→configuration task set.
sections.related_work: LLMs have been shown to synthesize configuration templates and to translate intent in controlled demonstrations; RAG and verifier-assisted loops improve grounding in domain QA and related tasks. Architectural proposals routinely recommend combining generative models with deterministic validators/simulators and human approval for safer NetOps workflows. However, rigorous, reproducible A/B-style experiments quantifying how much such deterministic validators plus simple automated repair reduce operational misconfiguration rates—under preregistered protocols—remain sparse. Survey, benchmark, and verification literature motivate controlled paired designs and deterministic validators to quantify concrete operational safety gains.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and design: The study (cand-2026-001-A-prereg-v1) specified a paired confirmatory design with N=300 deterministic task seeds and two within-task conditions: baseline (single-shot generation) and guarded (same initial generation guarded by a deterministic validator with ≤1 automated repair call). The primary estimand was the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline and the prespecified primary test was an exact McNemar test (α=0.05). Model and runtime sampling semantics (from the frozen model_configuration and execution manifests) are: declared_model_version = gpt-5-mini; temperature recorded as null (no stochastic temperature sampling applied); generation_semantics = "shared_initial_candidate"; independent_condition_generation = false. These settings mean the same initial sampled candidate was reused for the paired baseline/guarded conditions for each task (shared initial generation stage_count = 300; repair stage_count = 1; total hosted model calls recorded = 301). Practical implication: reusing an identical initial candidate across paired arms isolates the validator/repair intervention within pairs but increases within-pair correlation and thus reduces the number of discordant pairs available to the McNemar test; this correlation lowers the observable discordance and therefore the detectable signal for small absolute differences. Task bank and scoring: 300 synthetic intent→configuration pairs were deterministically generated by deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 with canonical reference answers; a frozen deterministic configuration validator/constraint checker (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) performed automated pass/fail scoring and produced per-task validator traces. Execution contract limited each task to one initial generation call and at most one repair call; all raw outputs, validator traces, repair prompts, and logs were recorded. The preregistration also documented planned sensitivity analyses and missingness treatments (complete_pair_primary and a failure-as-zero sensitivity), and a contamination-detection plan (deterministic exact/AST matching and near-duplicate thresholds).
sections.results: Execution and accounting: planned episodes = 600, completed episodes = 600, complete pairs = 300, model_calls_used = 301; no infrastructure/provider failures occurred and no preregistered deterministic exclusions/replacements were invoked. Contamination: the preregistered contamination_summary produced zero flagged items; deterministic_reconciliation reports all deterministic-consistency checks passed. Primary outcomes (archived analysis artifacts): baseline successes = 299/300 (99.667%); guarded successes = 300/300 (100.0%). Paired contingency table (guarded vs baseline): n11=299, n10=1, n01=0, n00=0. Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.00; absolute paired difference = 0.00333. Bootstrap (paired-percentile) 95% CI = [0.00, 0.01] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). Repair usage: a single repair-stage call occurred (repair stage count = 1) and produced the sole discordant correction in favor of guarded. Secondary analyses planned in the preregistration (repair success by failure category, subgroup stratification) are constrained by the single discordant observation and therefore inconclusive; all per-task traces and artifacts are archived for reproducibility.
sections.discussion: Why the preregistered hypothesis was not supported: the preregistration's power calculation assumed a much lower baseline pass rate (~0.40), so the target effect (50% relative reduction in fail rate, roughly an absolute +30% increase in pass rate) required substantial headroom. Observed baseline performance (299/300) left virtually no headroom, making the preregistered detectability target untestable in practice. Additionally, the runtime sampling semantics (shared_initial_candidate and temperature=null) increased within-pair correlation and reduced the number of discordant pairs available to the McNemar test, further limiting statistical sensitivity to small absolute differences. Operational interpretation: on this constrained synthetic task bank and with this single LLM, single-shot generation already achieved near-ceiling validity; the guarded pipeline deterministically fixed the one failure encountered but produced no statistically detectable improvement in the preregistered estimand. This null/near-ceiling result does not generalize to harder, adversarial, or production-like task banks where baseline error rates will likely be higher and validator coverage may be incomplete. Recommendations: evaluate harder and adversarial task suites, extend validator coverage, test multi-iteration repair loops, compare multiple model families and sampling regimes (non-null temperature and independent-condition generation), and measure runtime semantic consequences in emulators/simulators rather than relying solely on deterministic constraint checks.
sections.conclusion: In a preregistered paired experiment (N=300) using gpt-5-mini and a frozen deterministic validator with at most one automated repair iteration, baseline single-shot generation was near-ceiling (299/300) and the guarded pipeline produced 300/300 valid outputs; the small absolute gain produced one discordant pair corrected by repair but did not yield a statistically detectable improvement for the preregistered ≥50% relative reduction hypothesis. The study highlights the importance of matching preregistered power assumptions and sampling semantics to realistic baseline error rates and shows that deterministic validators can deterministically remedy some isolated failures even when baseline LLM outputs are already highly accurate on constrained synthetic tasks. Future experiments should target more challenging and adversarial conditions and broader model/validator configurations to reveal practical safety gains from verify-and-repair NetOps pipelines.

limitations: Synthetic task bank and constrained vendor-template scope limit external validity to broad production environments.
Single LLM (gpt-5-mini) and single validator implementation restrict generality across model families and validator designs.

Near-ceiling baseline performance (299/300) produced no practical headroom to detect the preregistered target effect (≥50% relative reduction) under the planned design; correlated paired sampling (shared_initial_candidate) further reduced discordant-pair counts and therefore statistical sensitivity.
Validation used deterministic configuration/constraint checks rather than full dynamic emulation of runtime semantic effects; runtime execution consequences remain unmeasured.
